query: For the paper "Generating Major Types of Chinese Classical Poetry in a Uniformed Framework" (arXiv: 2003.11528), answer this question: What are the types of chinese poetry that are generated?

drafts:
The paper generates two primary types of Chinese classical poetry: SHI (in its two major forms, Jueju and Lvshi) and CI (121 major forms, called Cipai), all with a single model [1].

Chinese classical poetry is classified into two primary categories, SHI and CI [5]. The proposed uniformed framework tries to generate the two major forms of SHI — Jueju and Lvshi — as well as 121 major forms (Cipai) of CI using a single model [1].

cited_sources.text: In fact, the research on the automatic generation of CI is just at the very beginning stage. In this paper, we propose a uniformed computational frame- work that tries to generate major types of Chinese classi- cal poems with two major forms of SHI, Jueju, and Lvshi, as well as 121 major forms (Cipai) of CI using a single model. Preliminary experimental results validate the ef- fectiveness of the proposed framework.

These three points form the universal principles for human poets to create Chinese classical poems. Chinese Classical poetry can be classiﬁed into two primary categories, SHI and CI. According to the statistical data from CCPC1.0, a Chinese Classical Poetry Corpus consist- ing of 834,902 poems in total (We believe it is almost a full collection of Chinese Classical poems). 92.87% poems in CCPC1.0 fall into the category of SHI and 7.13% fall into the category of CI.
